note: Writes Data/aircraft-doors.json: every door of the game's A320 (the FlightGear A320-200 model, Art/A320/A320.glb, as Art/A320/make_a320_fg.py builds it) measured on the model itself - no guessed numbers. Frame: the model's own cm - x its right, y aft, z up, the root at the nose wheel on the ground (glTF x, z, y * 100). Per door, from the door's own part (DoorL1/R1/L4/R4, Cargo1/2/3, their .Inner faces and .Placards, DoorHingeL1/R1/L2/R2): frame     the closed door's bounds skin      [x, y]: the middle of the sill on the outer skin; sill: its height; turn: degrees the skin there is turned from straight out (toward the tail; the cater truck, stairs and jetways square up to it) out       [x, y]: the skin's outward direction in plan (unit) hinge     the hinge line's middle (passenger doors: the hinge arm's forward pivot; cargo 1/2: the top edge; bulk: top edge) handle    out: the outside handle (hand IK to open and to close from outside), in: the inside handle (from the cabin/hold) passenger doors: the middle of the handle placard on the door (the decal island nearest the door's middle); cargo doors: the model has no handle part - the locking handle sits in the middle of the lower edge (Airbus layout), so 15 cm up the skin from the lower edge's middle outside   where a person stands outside the door, on the stair, jetway, catering or belt-loader top: 0.6 m out, sill height inside    where a person stands inside the open door: 0.6 m in (cabin floor / hold floor at the sill) dock      where the jetway's or stair's bumper, the cater box's or loader's front stops: 5 cm off the skin at the sill box: the model's bounds when measured; the game moves the points with the model's real size (GSEStairs.cpp, AircraftDoors.cpp). The order of "doors" is kept: 0 L1, 1 L4 (the stairs' front and rear door), then R1, R4, Cargo1, Cargo2, Cargo3. Run: python Tools/make_aircraft_doors.py  (then python Tools/make_aircraft_workpoints.py: the cargo door work points follow)
